title: The dth Fitting ideal detects smoothness in a pure-dimensional flat family
statement: Let $g:T\to B$ be a flat morphism of schemes [def-weil-flat-morphism], locally of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], and let $d\geq0$ be an integer. Assume every nonempty geometric fibre [def-weil-geometric-fibre] is equidimensional of dimension $d$ [def-kun-dimension]. Write $\Omega^1_{T/B}$ for the relative differential sheaf [def-sc-relative-differential-sheaf]. Let $Z_d\hookrightarrow T$ be the closed subscheme [def-weil-closed-immersion] cut out by $\operatorname{Fit}_d(\Omega^1_{T/B})$: on an affine chart with generators $\omega_1,\ldots,\omega_n$ of the differential module and relation module $K\subset A^n$, this is the ideal generated by the $(n-d)\times(n-d)$ minors of matrices with rows in $K$; for $d\geq n$ it is the unit ideal. These are the usual presentation-independent Fitting ideals, glued by localization; for $d=1$ this is [def-trf-first-fitting-singular-subscheme]. Then the locus $V\subseteq T$ where $g$ is smooth [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] is open, and $|Z_d|=|T|\setminus V$.
